newsitem.title: POLAND: Netherlands Queen Beatrix impresses Polish capital.
newsitem.headline: Netherlands Queen Beatrix impresses Polish capital.

text.p: Queen Beatrix of the Netherlands paid tribute to Poland's tragic past and its present economic progress on Wednesday, visiting World War Two monuments in Warsaw and showing considerable knowledge of its stock market.

On the first of three days in Poland with her consort Prince Claus, the Queen was the first crowned monarch to visit Warsaw's stock exchange, housed in what was the seat of the ruling Communist party before it fell from power in 1989.

Queen Beatrix, among the world's wealthier women, impressed bourse President Wieslaw Rozlucki by her familiarity with the three-tier market where Dutch investors have an estimated 23 percent of foreign-held shares, PAP news agency said.
"She is unusually to the point," it quoted him as saying.

The Queen broke with the usual practice of foreign dignitaries visiting the memorial to Warsaw's 1944 uprising against World War Two Nazi German occupiers, laying a wreath with her own hands rather than looking on soldiers doing so.
She also visited a memorial to the city's Jews, most of whom were murdered by the Nazis.

The royal couple lunched with President Aleksander Kwasniewski and the Queen strolled in the city's Old Town, reconstructed from wartime ruins, impressing onlookers with her extravagant pink hat crowned with flower petals.
Poland prizes its cordial ties with the Netherlands as a source of support for its NATO and European Union aspirations as well as because of increasingly healthy trade relations.

"Poland is the most interesting trading partner in central Europe for the Netherlands," Dutch Foreign Trade Minister Anneke van Dok-van Weele, also visiting Warsaw with a strong economic delegation, told reporters after a meeting with Finance minister Marek Belka.
"What we have to do now is co-operate as friends so as to be partners in the EU as soon as possible," she said.
Last year bilateral trade was $2.58 billion, with Polish imports from the Netherlands accounting for $1.41 billion.
Dutch investment reached $1.25 billion by end-1996, making the Netherlands Poland's fifth largest foreign investor, according to the Polish Agency for Foreign Investment.

Queen Beatrix is also due to visit Wroclaw in the west and the Baltic port city of Gdansk where she will meet Lech Walesa, who founded the Soviet bloc's first free trade union there in 1980 and is now an opposition politician.
